claim: The MAGE method. Scale creates the enduring reasoning problem; commodity intelligence changes its economics. Modeling makes consequential engineering properties explicit and available to analysis; Alignment makes selected obligations enforceable. Governance conversion turns recurring failures and judgment into models and controls that future work can reuse, so engineering effort can accumulate instead of being paid for again.

topology.description: Restored the abstract-or-reconstruct state phrase and causal edge annotations for scarcity, exposed properties, economic change, and future value versus upkeep. Retained Modeling and Alignment gray modes, dashed churn alternatives, governance feedback, and dotted scope feedback.
native_draw_commands: \draw[edge] (s0) -- node[lab,right,inner sep=1pt] {makes judgment scarce at scale} (s1);

required_terms: and intent explicit at useful scales
bw_encoding: Black 0.9 bp connectors and arrowheads; one light-gray role for the two principles; dashed outline marks the prediction.
redesign: Author-approved B&W-only facing-page redesign, November 9. Claim numbers and vocabulary align the diagram with the prose; parallel principles and a two-target conversion loop preserve their distinct roles. The broader reorganization prediction is separate from the mechanism flow.
alt: Claims one and two motivate parallel Modeling and Alignment principles. Both guide and govern engineering work. Recurring failures and judgment lead to governance conversion, whose feedback adapts models and controls. Later benefit makes durable structure engineering capital. Claim six is a separate prediction about the reorganization of engineering work.
governance_revision_reason: The overview should name constraints, sensors, and gates; its description distinguishes restrictions, evidence, and admission.

checks.text: Engineering capital when later work keeps benefiting.
